words.prose: {{ar:ثُمَّ}} ({{tr:thumma}}) does not merely open a new sentence; it moves the prior fire-contact of 87:12 into a further stage. Because it stands before the whole paired negation, the later stage is not just failure to die but the full condition in which both death and life are denied. The particle therefore makes the punishment feel sequenced and intensified: first the greater fire is entered, then its interior condition is disclosed. Its short opening beat also launches the first negation quickly, so release through death is blocked before the clause finishes naming the whole trap.

topics.headline: later stage after fire-contact
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the neither-death-nor-life condition is presented as the developed stage after entry into the greater fire, not as a detached description.
topics.reason: QAC identifies the word as a sequencer, and attachment evidence places it before the first negated verbal predicate continuing the punishment scene from 87:12.

topics.headline: scope over the full neither-nor frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the sequence particle governs the whole paired denial, so the subsequent stage is both denied death and denied life.
topics.reason: The attachment layer marks the first and second negated predicates as coordinated, with the opening sequencer preceding that coordinated frame.

topics.headline: boundary into interior stasis
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ayah boundary as a turn from entering the fire to being held inside its unresolved condition.
topics.reason: The particle opens 87:13 while attachment evidence links the following clause to the locative fire-domain, supporting a boundary shift rather than an independent maxim.

words.gloss_range: negative particle over the first imperfect verb; here it denies death as release while opening a paired neither-nor construction

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the first imperfect verb negated by the particle

words.prose: The first {{ar:لَا}} ({{tr:lā}}) directly targets {{ar:يَمُوتُ}} ({{tr:yamūtu}}), so death itself is the first endpoint closed. Because the verb remains an indicative imperfect, the line states an ongoing punishment condition rather than commanding someone not to die. This matters for the reader: non-death is not mercy here, since the syntax first blocks death as release and then waits for the second negation to remove life as an alternative. The repeated negative sound makes the two exits distinct in recitation instead of letting one broad negation blur them together.

topics.headline: death denied as first endpoint
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that death is blocked first, so the most obvious endpoint or release is removed before life is separately addressed.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence identify the particle as negating the first imperfect predicate, with the paired negation preserved across both predicates.

topics.headline: condition, not prohibition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the line describes deprivation inside punishment; it is not an instruction forbidding the subject to die.
topics.reason: The verb is an imperfect indicative under negative particle scope, and the local syntax reports the fire-domain condition rather than an imperative frame.

topics.headline: first beat of double closure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the first negator as the opening beat of a staged deprivation whose full force arrives with the later repeated negator.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence marks the two negated predicates as coordinated, so the first negator legitimately functions as the first member of a paired neither-nor frame.

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: parallel punishment formula with the same death-life denial

words.prose: {{ar:يَمُوتُ}} ({{tr:yamūtu}}) names the first withheld endpoint. The verb is objectless and intransitive, so the clause denies the subject's own dying rather than making him an agent or an object of killing. Its imperfect form under {{ar:لَا}} ({{tr:lā}}) keeps death continually unrealized inside the fire-domain, not merely absent at one past moment. The broader {{ar:م و ت}} ({{tr:m-w-t}}) field can include deadness, caused death, deathlike posture, and even seeking death, but the local Form I narrows the payoff to basic death as completion: what would normally terminate exposure is refused. The paired verb {{ar:يَحْيَىٰ}} ({{tr:yaḥyā}}) shares the ya- imperfect onset with it, while this word's terminal t sound gives death a hard closure that the semantics refuse. Read after the greater fire of 87:12 and beside the exact formula in 20:74, the familiar death-life polarity has become a punitive anti-cycle rather than a normal passage through death and life such as 2:28.

topics.headline: subject's own death-event denied
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the clause denies the sufferer's own dying inside the fire, not an action done to another or a newly named agent.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence marks the verb as objectless and intransitive with an implicit 3ms subject continued from the prior discourse.

topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices death not as a one-time non-event but as an endpoint kept unavailable throughout the punishment scene.
topics.reason: The local form is an imperfect active verb under negation; contextual polarity also shows this root-form often occurs under negation or scope, supporting the durative withholding reading.

topics.reason: V4 lists broader death and deadness branches, but the aligned local word is Form I intransitive, so derivative mechanisms such as seeking death or deathlike becoming remain background pressure rather than the selected local sense.

topics.reason: The two verbs are visible as paired imperfects in coordinated predicates; the sound observation is secondary but grounded in the local surfaces.

words.prose: {{ar:فِيهَا}} ({{tr:fīhā}}) makes the prior {{ar:ٱلنَّارَ ٱلْكُبْرَىٰ}} ({{tr:al-nāra al-kubrā}}) from 87:12 remain grammatically present without being renamed. The feminine suffix points back to that fire, while {{ar:فِي}} ({{tr:fī}}) puts the subject inside it as the shared domain of the two denied predicates. Placed between {{ar:يَمُوتُ}} ({{tr:yamūtu}}) and {{ar:يَحْيَىٰ}} ({{tr:yaḥyā}}), the word turns enclosure into the hinge of the antithesis: death and life both fail in the same recalled container. That same containment specifies the greatness of the fire named in 87:12: its interior condition is neither death nor life. The compact fusion of preposition and pronoun makes containment and antecedent recall inseparable on the surface, and the long final sound also helps tie the enclosure to the final life-word.

topics.reason: The attachment layer makes the prepositional phrase the locative complement of the first verb, while the coordinated second predicate shares the same punishment frame.

topics.headline: locative hinge in the antithesis
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the locative in the middle of the two opposite verbs, making enclosure the pivot rather than an afterthought.
topics.reason: The surface order places the locative after the first negated verb and before the coordinated second predicate, matching the CRITICAL structural claim.

topics.headline: fused containment and long-ā link
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the compact word binds containment to pronoun recall, while its long ending audibly links the enclosure to the final denied life.
topics.reason: The local surface visibly combines preposition and suffix and ends in a long vowel before the closing life verb; the claim is formal and phonetic, not a new semantic branch.

topics.reason: The fire antecedent from 87:12 is strongly licensed for the pronoun, and the locative phrase governs the local punishment condition.

words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) is small, but it decides how the second denial is read. It coordinates {{ar:لَا يَحْيَىٰ}} ({{tr:lā yaḥyā}}) with the first negated predicate, so life is not a new topic after death but the paired counter-exit within the same suspended state. The conjunction adds the expected opposite and at the same time sharpens the contrast: after death is refused, life is not left as an available residue. Its entry before the second {{ar:لَا}} ({{tr:lā}}) gives the final denial its own audible start while keeping it bound to the first.

topics.headline: second denial coordinated with first
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the life-denial belongs to the same suspended condition as the death-denial, not to a later separate scene.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence marks the second predicate as coordinated with the first through the conjunction.

topics.headline: opposites bound under one frame

topics.reason: The coordinated verbs are the death-life pair, and contextual collocation identifies the two roots as frequent partners in this form class.

topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the second half as both linked to the first negation and audibly launched as its own closing beat.
topics.reason: The surface conjunction appears as the onset of the second negated unit, making the formal completion claim local and bounded.

words.prose: The second {{ar:لَا}} ({{tr:lā}}) prevents a false inference: if the subject does not die, that still does not mean he lives. By repeating the particle before {{ar:يَحْيَىٰ}} ({{tr:yaḥyā}}), the ayah gives life its own predicate-level negation rather than letting it be a weak implication from the first clause. This turns non-death into punitive non-life, completing the syntactic trap in which the first exit is death and the second is meaningful life. The repeated open sound also balances the two denials before the final long ending of the life verb.

words.prose: {{ar:يَحْيَىٰ}} ({{tr:yaḥyā}}) closes the ayah on the word that should have been the relief opposite of death. Instead, under the second {{ar:لَا}} ({{tr:lā}}), life is continually unrealized for the same unspoken subject who was denied death. The objectless Form I verb denies the subject's own life-state, not an act of reviving someone else. The wider {{ar:ح ي ي}} ({{tr:ḥ-y-y}}) field includes vitality, reviving, sparing alive, recognition through greeting, and true life, but local grammar narrows the selected sense to living itself while letting those branches sharpen what is withheld. The contrasts with the same punishment formula in 20:74, true life in 29:64, the death-life sequence in 2:28, and later worldly life in 87:16 make the end sharper: the afterlife condition here is excluded from true vitality and freezes the normal death-life movement. Within the surah, the contained final denial also becomes the negative foil for the next ayah's success in 87:14. The final long sound gives formal closure while the meaning refuses the consolation that closure might suggest.

topics.reason: The local word is a Form I imperfect active verb under a repeated negative particle, not a perfect, imperative, or causative reviving form.

topics.reason: V4 supports many accepted life-family branches, but the local intransitive Form I imperfect selects living/vitality; greeting, sparing-alive, true-life, and derivational dispute rows are preserved as narrowed semantic pressure.

topics.headline: relief opposite turned into deprivation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that life arrives as the expected opposite of death, but the second negation turns that expected relief into the final denied possibility.
topics.reason: The local life verb is coordinated with the death verb, and contextual collocation shows these roots forming a strong death-life pair in this form class.

topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the denied life here contrasts with true life in 29:64, the death-life sequence in 2:28, the same punishment formula in 20:74, and the later worldly-life mention in 87:16.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows supply concrete references, and none conflicts with the local grammar; they function as formulaic and thematic contrasts rather than governing the local parse.

topics.headline: open closing sound, withheld life
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah lands on an open long ending associated with the life verb while the semantics deny life, so formal closure carries unresolved meaning.
topics.reason: The final alif maqṣūrah and closing position are visible in the local word; the sound claim is formal and does not create a separate lexical sense.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The balanced construction la yamutu fiha wa-la yahya coordinates two present-tense negations inside one location, with thumma presenting the condition as a result.
baseline_models.mechanism: The first negation prevents the loss of vitality from reaching death, while the second prevents persistence from becoming animate life. The subject is therefore held between terminal cessation and functioning animation rather than alternating normally between them.

activation_trace.role: Loss of vitality supplies the terminal endpoint that the first negation refuses to let complete.
Animate existence supplies the positive endpoint that the second negation withholds.

changed_reading.before: The line is a bare paradox: he does not die and is not alive.
changed_reading.after: The line specifies an imposed interval in which death never finishes and life never becomes functioning animation.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The same double negation can distinguish continued exposure from the qualities that make continuation count as life.
baseline_models.mechanism: Negated death removes quiescent shutdown, while negated life removes benefit and saving good. What remains is duration without rest, welfare, rescue, or flourishing.

activation_trace.role: Death-like stillness, sleep, or wearing out supplies a possible shutdown that la yamutu denies.
Life as benefit, good, and rescue supplies the qualitative life that wa-la yahya denies.

changed_reading.before: Not dying appears equivalent to continuing to live.
changed_reading.after: Mere continuation is severed from life: the subject cannot shut down, yet receives none of life's benefit or rescue.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The paired imperfect verbs permit a process reading in which neither a collapse nor a renewal ever occurs.
baseline_models.mechanism: A death-word branch names a swoon or seizure from which one later recovers, while a life-word branch names earth renewed through rain and growth. Negating both yields an anti-cycle: no temporary collapse that grants interruption and no regenerative return.

activation_trace.role: A recoverable faint or seizure supplies an episodic collapse whose interruption is denied.
Rain-driven renewal and fresh growth supply the restorative phase that is also denied.

changed_reading.before: The verse denies two static states, death and life.
changed_reading.after: The verse can also deny both phases of a restorative rhythm: no merciful lapse and no return to freshness.

context_deltas.mechanism: Creation is followed by setting right, measure by guidance: each earlier pair moves a thing toward form, limit, and direction. Against that ordered movement, the focus state becomes an anti-completion deliberately situated within the same order, a creature brought to a condition that reaches neither terminal loss nor positive telos.

activation_trace.role: The loss-of-vitality endpoint remains visibly blocked in the focus.
Functioning animation remains the equally blocked positive endpoint.
Completed and proportioned formation supplies the context's first image of arrival at integrity.
Intrinsic straightness and completion turns creation into directed completion rather than bare origination.
A measured limit supplies the notion that things ordinarily attain a determined bound.
Gentle direction toward a path supplies telic movement, sharpening the focus as its punitive inversion.

structural_cues: 87:2-3 contains two compact fa-linked sequences: creation to setting-right and measuring to guidance.
The focus begins with thumma, presenting its double negation as a reached consequence even while both ordinary endpoints remain unreached.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies ordered completion, limit, direction, and then two blocked endpoints; I infer that the focus is a deliberately measured anti-telos. A live alternative is that 87:2-3 establishes agency only and does not specify the mechanics of punishment.

changed_reading.before: The neither-dead-nor-alive state looks like an accidental logical gap.
changed_reading.after: It becomes a measured anti-completion: an assigned outcome whose punishment is precisely the failure to attain either kind of completion.

context_deltas.mechanism: The pasture sequence supplies a material cycle: emergence, usable growth, deliberate transformation, then withered debris. The focus roots contain matching images of revived earth and dead land, but both are negated. The punished subject is unlike vegetation that can complete decay and unlike earth that can receive renewal: the cycle arrests while exposure continues.

activation_trace.role: Dead, unusable land supplies the completed lifeless condition that the first negation blocks.
Earth revived into fresh growth supplies the regenerative condition that the second negation blocks.
Emergence to the outside initiates the visible material cycle.
Grazable pasture supplies a living and useful phase rather than life in the abstract.
Causing a thing to become a new state makes the decay transition explicit.
Pasture reduced to brittle waste supplies the normally completed death-side of the cycle.

structural_cues: 87:4-5 moves in sequence from brought-out pasture to its being made dark, withered debris.
The focus repeats the same life/death polarity but negates both poles.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a completed vegetal transformation and focus branches for revived and dead land; I map that material cycle onto the human double negation and infer arrested transformation. The live alternative is that the pasture cycle functions only as a general sign of power, not as an analogy for the focus state.

changed_reading.before: The focus describes an abstract suspension between biological states.
changed_reading.after: It also pictures matter denied both ecological outcomes: it cannot finish into inert waste and cannot re-enter fertile renewal.

context_deltas.mechanism: The context distinguishes loss of remembrance, received reminder, beneficial response, fear-filled recollection, and deliberate withdrawal. This revises nondeath as awareness that is not extinguished and nonlife as awareness that never becomes beneficial response. The subject remains available to apprehension but closed to transformation.

activation_trace.role: Deadness of heart and understanding supplies the cognitive extinction that la yamutu can be heard to withhold.
Life as benefit and rescue supplies the fruitful responsiveness that wa-la yahya withholds.
Loss of an item from remembrance supplies the cognitive disappearance explicitly negated earlier in the context.
A reminder designed to reactivate memory supplies the offered stimulus.
Benefit as the opposite of harm distinguishes fruitful reception from mere exposure.
Fear joined with awe supplies the affect that lets one recipient actually remember.
Active distancing and withdrawal supplies the wretched recipient's contrary response.

structural_cues: 87:6-11 repeatedly alternates retention, reminder, useful response, remembrance, and avoidance.
The avoidant subject of 87:11 is carried through the fire clause of 87:12 into the two present-tense negations.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a response chain and focus branches for cognitive deadness and beneficial life; I infer that punishment preserves apprehension while preventing fruitful integration. A live alternative is that the focus verbs remain wholly somatic and the remembrance sequence characterizes antecedent conduct only.

changed_reading.before: The subject is biologically suspended but his awareness is unspecified.
changed_reading.after: He remains conscious enough that oblivion cannot release him, yet never becomes alive in the sense of receiving benefit, rescue, or transformative remembrance.

context_deltas.mechanism: The immediately preceding fire is not only a location but an acting medium: one meets its heat, and a branch of the same root depicts fire kindled to work or shape a thing. The double negation makes that action nonterminal. Fire can continually diminish strength and act on the subject, but it neither completes destruction nor produces restored animation.

activation_trace.role: The deadening of force supplies what the fire can repeatedly do without achieving final death.
Animate functioning supplies the positive condition that repeated processing never restores.
Direct encounter with fire and its heat supplies the immediate causal medium.
Kindling heat to work or set a thing supplies a process image rather than a merely static location.
Burning fire and its mark make ongoing material exposure concrete.
Magnitude intensifies the acting medium while making its failure to terminate the subject more striking.

structural_cues: 87:12 identifies the subject through his encounter with the great fire; 87:13 follows with thumma.
The pronoun in fiha keeps both negated processes inside that fire, and both verbs remain imperfect.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies contact with fire, a heat-shaping branch, magnitude, thumma, fiha, and durative verb forms; I infer repeated nonterminal processing. A live alternative is a static description of one permanent state with no implied cycles of action.

changed_reading.before: Fire is the backdrop for an otherwise unexplained neither-dead-nor-alive condition.
changed_reading.after: Fire is the mechanism of an unfinished process: it continually acts and deadens, while the two negations prevent either destruction or restored life from closing the process.

context_deltas.mechanism: The verses after the focus define a positive trajectory as surviving success, growth or purification, recollection, and worship. Distant but live focus branches then yield an orientation reading: the subject neither yields to truth under the death-root nor comes forward under the life-root. His stasis is relational, the inability to enter the successful trajectory set immediately beside him.

activation_trace.role: Submission to truth supplies a branch-distant yielding that the negated focus verb refuses.
The summons to come or approach supplies positive movement that the second negation blocks.
Success joined with survival supplies the attained condition contrasted with suspended nonlife.
Growth and increase supply a positive developmental trajectory.
Active recollection supplies the inward turn that precedes worship.
Specific worship supplies the outward act completing the positive trajectory.

structural_cues: 87:14-15 immediately reverses the focus's two negations with a compact sequence of success, self-purification, remembrance, and prayer.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a positive post-focus trajectory plus focus branches of yielding and approach; I infer that wa-la yahya can carry blocked orientation as well as absent vitality. A live alternative is that these remote branch senses should remain only analogical and that the contrast is simply between two populations.

changed_reading.before: The subject cannot occupy the state called life.
changed_reading.after: He cannot move toward life: he neither yields nor approaches the growth-remembrance-worship sequence that follows.

context_deltas.mechanism: The later comparison separates chosen worldly life, superior good, and greater permanence into distinct values. That separation resolves the focus paradox without dissolving it: la yamutu grants ongoing duration, while wa-la yahya denies life as benefit and good. Persistence is present, but the evaluative content that would make it life is absent.

activation_trace.role: Blocked loss of vitality supplies continued duration at the focus.
Life as benefit, good, and rescue supplies the quality denied despite that duration.
Preferential choice makes life an evaluated object rather than a synonym for bare persistence.
The named worldly life activates the benefit-bearing sense of the same focus root.
The lower or worldly qualifier bounds the preferred life as one mode rather than life as mere existence.
Laterness supplies the contrasting temporal domain in which quality and duration are compared.
Beneficial good supplies an explicit evaluative axis separate from duration.
Continuance and permanence supply the temporal axis, proving that remaining and living need not be identical.

structural_cues: 87:16 names life as what is preferred; 87:17 answers with two separate comparatives, better and more lasting.
Placed after 87:13, the comparison lexically disaggregates life, good, and duration.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies separate terms for chosen life, beneficial superiority, and permanence; I infer that the focus distributes those properties across its negations, retaining duration while denying benefit. A live alternative is the strictly biological reading in which 87:16-17 only compares realms.

changed_reading.before: If he does not die, calling him not alive is simply paradoxical.
changed_reading.after: The paradox becomes diagnostic: he remains, but remaining has been emptied of benefit, rescue, and every quality for which life is chosen.

context_deltas.mechanism: The closing appeal to repeated written sheets and an earlier source can extend the focus from an instantaneous sensation to a stable, transmissible outcome. The first-text root also carries return to an eventual outcome, allowing the suspended state to be read as an invariant terminus repeatedly attested rather than a passing anomaly.

activation_trace.role: The blocked terminal endpoint supplies one half of the stable proposition.
The blocked animate endpoint supplies the proposition's other half.
A written sheet supplies durable inscription rather than transient speech.
The repeated written-sheet cue reinforces transmission across named prior witnesses.
Return to an eventual outcome activates the focus as a fixed terminus carried by earlier teaching.

structural_cues: 87:18-19 repeats the scroll term and closes the surah by naming earlier scrolls.
The deictic hadha may gather the preceding teaching, though its exact scope is not grammatically forced to be 87:13 alone.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies durable writing, repetition, priority, and a branch of eventual outcome; I infer that the focus condition is presented as a stable invariant. The materially live alternative is that hadha refers only to the final exhortation or to the surah generally, so this delta remains exploratory.

changed_reading.before: The suspended state is experienced moment by moment inside the fire.
changed_reading.after: It is additionally framed as a fixed outcome, durable enough to recur as an inherited and written warning.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it reads nondeath through the social-legal image of sparing rather than through biology. It remains anchored in the focus's negated death/life pair and is activated by a later branch where keeping someone alive can be pardon; downstream prose should call it an anti-clemency analogy, not claim that the verb lexically means pardon here.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: La yamutu can resemble being withheld from killing, but wa-la yahya immediately strips that withholding of the life normally secured by sparing.

activation_trace.role: Literal loss of life supplies the killing endpoint from which the subject is withheld.
Sparing someone alive supplies the expected merciful consequence that the second negation cancels.
Preservation as pardon or merciful sparing exposes how punitive mere preservation can become when detached from life.

changed_reading.before: Not dying looks like preservation and therefore like a lesser mercy.
changed_reading.after: The subject is formally spared the killing endpoint, but the paired denial of life turns sparing into its punitive opposite: preservation without mercy.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it cross-connects remote hunting and trap branches rather than the dominant fire and death senses. It remains anchored by fiha, the immediate fire clause, the double negation, and the focus branch concerning uncertainty over whether wounded game has died; downstream prose should present it only as a material analogy for enclosure and unresolved status.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The locative fiha encloses a subject whose death can never be ascertained as complete and whose life never resumes.

activation_trace.role: Checking whether wounded game is dead supplies an image of terminal status remaining perpetually unresolved.
Animate functioning supplies the recovery that never resolves the uncertainty in the other direction.
Snares and traps supply the enclosing mechanism through which the fire can be imaged as holding its quarry.

changed_reading.before: The subject is simply located in fire.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, the fire behaves like a snare holding wounded prey in an endlessly unresolved state: never certifiably dead, never restored to animate life.

strongest_changes: The pasture-to-waste sequence turns the focus into an arrested material cycle denied both completed decay and renewal.
The immediate fire clause makes the double negation a nonterminal process in an acting medium, not only a static paradox.
The remembrance-and-avoidance sequence permits preserved awareness without beneficial response.
The distinction among worldly life, good, and permanence makes duration without life semantically coherent while preserving its horror.
summary.what_was_special: The two negations did not collapse into one compromise reading. They supported coexisting temporal, qualitative, ecological, cognitive, processual, and relational models, with remote sparing and trap branches retained as contained discoveries rather than promoted to lexical conclusions.
remaining_uncertainties: The swoon, submission, approach, sparing, and hunting branches are form- or domain-distant from the direct focus verbs and must remain exploratory.
The repeated fire process is an inference from sequence, location, and imperfect aspect; the packet also permits a static permanent-state reading.
The scope of hadha in 87:18 may be the final exhortation or the surah generally rather than this focus condition specifically.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Suspended negation between death and life.** Lexical evidence: م و ت B001/B012 (loss of vitality; stillness), ح ي ي B003/B013 (living creature; life as saving good). Structural cue: paired negations hold the subject inside the fire after 87:12. Assigned role: death is denied as release; life is denied as benefit. Abductive move: punishment can suspend ordinary endings and goods. Reading change: the ayah describes not paradox for its own sake but a blocked transition-state.

2. **Dead land versus rain-life.** Lexical evidence: م و ت B003 (dead land/lifeless property), ح ي ي B002 (earth alive by rain and growth), ر ع ي B001 in 87:4 and غ ث و B002 in 87:5. Structural cue: pasture lives then dries; here the person neither dies nor lives. Assigned role: ecological life/death cycles are withheld in the fire. Abductive move: natural renewal is a mercy not available inside the punitive state. Reading change: the fire becomes anti-ecology: no fertile death, no living renewal.

3. **Submission refused.** Lexical evidence: م و ت B013 (submission to truth), ذ ك ر B009 in 87:9, خ ش ي B001/B002 in 87:10. Structural cue: the one who avoids reminder reaches this suspended state. Assigned role: "does not die" may also imply he never performs the truth-yielding death/submission that would have answered reminder. Abductive move: existential suspension mirrors moral non-submission. Reading change: the negated death includes a missed surrender, not only biological continuation.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 87:14 immediately reversed the suspended state: success/purification offers genuine life-direction after the non-life of fire. The earlier pasture cycle also made this ayah feel like an interruption of normal life/death renewal.

reader_b.activated_readings_md:
1. **Suspended negation between death and life.** Lexical evidence: موت B001 loss of life/vitality; حيي B003 animate living being. Structural cue: repeated لا around two opposed verbs inside "فيها." Assigned role: موت and حياة are both denied, trapping the subject in a non-resolution. Abductive move: the packet supplies the life/death opposition; I infer suspension from double negation. Reading change: punishment is not simple death but blocked completion of either state.

2. **Deadness of heart and life as saving benefit.** Lexical evidence: موت B006 deadness of heart; حيي B013 life as benefit/saving good; نفع B001 benefit in 87:9. Structural cue: the avoidant refused beneficial reminder before the fire. Assigned role: he loses the benefit-life offered by reminder yet does not receive release by death. Abductive move: the packet supplies benefit-life and heart-deadness; I infer that rejection produces inner lifelessness before final suspension. Reading change: the ayah becomes moral-existential, not only biological.

3. **No regeneration after the pasture cycle.** Lexical evidence: حيي B002 earth brought alive by rain/growth; غثو B002 dried pasture/refuse in 87:5; موت B003 dead land/lifeless property. Structural cue: earlier vegetation moved from pasture to refuse; here life/death are both denied. Assigned role: the ecological cycle is broken in the fire. Abductive move: the packet supplies land revived by rain and dead land; I infer that this state lacks the rain-growth renewal available in creation. Reading change: "nor live" means no new greening, no productive return.

4. **False submission and unreleased truth.** Lexical evidence: موت B013 submission to truth and B011 feigned humility; ذكر B009 reminder; خشي B001 awe. Structural cue: the one who avoided reminder contrasts with the one who fears. Assigned role: موت's submission branch reveals the missing act: he neither truly submits nor truly exits. Abductive move: the packet supplies submission and feigned deadness; I infer that avoidance leaves him unable to perform the death-to-truth that would have saved him. Reading change: the ayah encodes failed surrender, not only torment.
reader_b.retrospective_surprises_md: 87:14 immediately reversed the suspension: "قد أفلح من تزكى" shows the positive path where growth/purity succeeds. 87:16-17 added that the avoided life is paradoxical: choosing الحياة الدنيا can end in a state that is neither death nor life.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Both terminal closure and beneficial life are denied.** `م و ت/B001` is loss of vitality and life, while `ح ي ي/B013` is life as benefit, saving good, or rescue from destruction. The balanced negations follow exposure to fire and precede `أَفْلَحَ`, `خَيْرٌ`, and `أَبْقَىٰ`. Death would terminate the process; life would convert it into benefit. I infer those functional roles from the contrasted sequel. The ayah reads as exclusion from both closure and rescue, not as a simple paradox of biological status.
2. **The state is nonproductive suspension.** `م و ت/B012` gives stillness or lifeless inactivity, while `ح ي ي/B002` gives earth brought alive through rain and fresh growth. Later `ز ك و/B001` supplies increase and `ب ق ي/B001` enduring continuation, making productive renewal visible by contrast. The two negations block both settled stillness and regenerative growth. I infer that what remains is ongoing but sterile agitation. The reading changes from an abstract midpoint into a process that neither comes to rest nor yields new life.
3. **Exploratory: refusal to yield becomes fixed.** `م و ت/B013` is submission to truth, a dormant branch activated by reminder, recollection, and avoidance in 87:9–11. Negating `يَمُوتُ` can therefore add the image of one who still does not yield, while negating `يَحْيَىٰ` denies the benefit that yielding might open. The primary death sense remains supplied by `م و ت/B001`; this secondary layer depends on root resonance rather than the immediate form. It makes the condition a frozen continuation of the earlier avoidance, not merely an imposed environment.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 87:14’s purification-growth and 87:17’s good persistence corrected an undifferentiated “endless life” reading. They show exactly what the fixed state lacks: productive renewal and beneficial continuance. findings.text: Ölümün kapanışı da hayatın kurtarıcı yararı da engellendiği için durum iki hal arasında çözümsüz bir askıda kalıştır.
Toprağın yeniden canlanması çağrışımı da reddedildiğinden, bu süreklilik dinlenmeye varamayan ve yeni hayat üretemeyen kısır bir süreçtir.
Öğüdü reddeden kişi, kalbin ölüleşmesiyle kurtarıcı hayatı yitirmiş fakat ölümle serbest kalamamış halde görünür.
Ölümün teslim olma çağrışımı, kişinin ateşte bile gerçeğe boyun eğmeyen önceki kaçınmasını sürdürdüğünü düşündürür.

concept_map.definition: Canlıdaki güç ve yaşamın sona ermesi, yani yaşam durumunun karşıtına geçmesidir. Ölüm türleri, söz konusu yaşam türlerine göre ayrılabilir.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi yağmuru toprağı yaşatan neden olarak adlandırır ve bu anlamı verimli toprak, taze bitki, yağmura kavuşan topluluk ve otlanan hayvanlarla somutlaştırır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Yağmur ve toprak canlılığına ilişkin temel adlandırma, toprağı verimli bulma ve bir topluluğun yağmurla ota kavuşması gibi yapıya bağlı kullanımlardan ayrı tutulur.

concept_map.definition: Yağmurun toprağı canlandırması, verim ve taze bitki meydana getirmesidir; yağmurun kendisi de bu yaşatıcı etkiden ötürü adlandırılır. Toprağı bu durumda bulmak ve bir topluluğun yağmurla bol ota kavuşması yapıya bağlı uzantılardır.

facets.statement: Yağmur, toprağa canlılık verdiği ve onu ölüm görünümünden çıkardığı için bu adla anılır.

Toprağı verimli bulmak veya bir topluluğun yağmur ve bol ota kavuşması yalnız belirli yapılarda anlatılır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar yağmurun toprağı canlandırdığı konusunda birleşir; verim, taze bitki ve hayvanların otla güçlenmesi bu etkinin sonuçları olarak aktarılır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesinin baskın yönü ruh, duyum veya canlılık taşıyan varlıktır; ancak aynı ifade ayrıca bitmeyen gerçek yaşamı da ayrı bir kullanım olarak verir. Dal korunabilir, fakat varlık adı ile sonsuz yaşam okuması tek bir çekirdekmiş gibi birleştirilmemelidir.

source_note.SI: Biçim, kişinin yaşamını değil doğrudan yüzünü adlandırır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi yaşam sözünü yarar ve iyilik için kullanır; yaptırımın öldürmeyi caydırmasıyla toplumu korumasını ve birini yok olmaktan kurtarmayı bu değer alanının özel gerçekleşmeleri olarak açıklar.

lexicalization_scope.note: Genel yarar ve iyilik okuması ile yaptırım, kurtarma ve çocuğu yaşatan besin gibi belirli yapılara bağlı kullanımlar birbirinden ayrılır.

concept_map.definition: Yarar, iyilik veya yok olmaktan koruma sağlayan sonuçtur; özellikle karşılık yaptırımının öldürmeyi caydırarak insanları koruması ve birini yıkımdan kurtarmak bu değerin özel gerçekleşmeleridir.

facets.statement: Yarar ve iyilik, yaşam sözünün bu dalda kazandığı değer çekirdeğidir.
Karşılık yaptırımının öldürmeyi caydırıp insanları koruması, yararın toplumsal ve koruyucu gerçekleşmesidir.
Birini yok olmaktan kurtarmak, yaşamı koruyan yararın doğrudan eylem uzantısıdır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar yaşam sözünün yarar ve iyilik değeri taşıdığını bildirir; caydırıcı yaptırımın insanları koruması ve yok olmaktan kurtarma bu değerin açıklanan uygulamalarıdır.

concept_gloss.text: yarar, iyilik ve yok olmaktan koruma
concept_gloss.applicability: Değer çekirdeğini, caydırıcı korumayı ve kurtarma sonucunu birlikte anlatır.

error_profile.preserves: Yararı, iyiliği ve yaşamı koruyan sonucu eksiksiz korur.

error_profile.loses: Genel iyilik anlamını ve tek bir kişiyi kurtarma kullanımını bütünüyle kapsamaz.

error_profile.preserves: Yok olmaktan kurtarma eylemini ve koruyucu sonucu korur.
error_profile.loses: Genel yarar ile toplumsal caydırma boyutlarını kapsamaz.

neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Bu dal yararı yaşamın korunması ve kurtarma üzerinden kurar; komşu dal yaşamla ilgisi bulunmayan bütün yarar türlerine açıktır.

neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Bu dal öldürmenin karşılığı olan yaptırımın yaşam koruyucu sonucunu anlatır; komşu dal daha hafif ve eğitici cezayı anlatır.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Yok olmaktan kurtarma ve yaşamı caydırma yoluyla koruma bu dalın özel içeriğidir.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Kötülüğün karşıtı olan ve istenen her türlü genel iyilik komşu dalın geniş alanıdır.
neighbor_distinctions.gloss: yaşamı koruyan iyilik ile genel iyilik
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İki dal olumlu, yararlı ve istenir sonucu ifade edebilir.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Bu dal iyiliği yaşamı koruma ve kurtarma bağıyla sınırlar; komşu dal bütün yararlı ve erdemli sonuçları kapsar.

A root listed in dropped_roots is a deliberate scoping decision, not a missing source.
